note: This is a deliberately-vulnerable HTB lab app. Intended exploit chain is LDAP-injection auth bypass (app/sanitize.py fullwidth-char bypass, app/ldap_auth.py filter injection) -> privileged session -> Jinja2 SSTI RCE (app/ssti_blacklist.py + app/ssti_render.py, via documented ~-concat/tab bypass). Scores and reasons below focus on GENUINE UNINTENDED gaps: places where the app's own defenses are weaker than the design spec intended, or where an attacker reaches the SSTI sink with MORE access than the designed chain grants.

ranked_files.reason: UNINTENDED, empirically confirmed: is_blocked()'s regex `\{\{.*?\}\}` is not Jinja-lexer-aware and stops at the first literal '}}', including one embedded inside a quoted string. Payload `{{("}}"~"").__class__.__mro__[1].__subclasses__()}}` scans as fragment `{{("}}` (no banned tokens) yet Jinja's real lexer honors the quoting and evaluates the full expression -- is_blocked() returns False and render_report_template() returns the full class-subtree list with zero context required. This is a COMPLETE blacklist bypass (no tab trick, no space-avoidance cleverness needed) that is strictly stronger than the design-documented '~-concat + tab' bypass -- prove/kill: confirm this reaches os.popen/subprocess via __subclasses__ indexing for full RCE beyond info-disclosure.
signals: non-greedy match terminates early inside quoted string
verified bypass renders __mro__/__subclasses__ with empty context

ranked_files.reason: Single entry-point file: owns both attacker-reachable routes (/login, /admin/report-template), the sole authorization check (`session.get("is_privileged")`), and wires raw request.form input into both the LDAP sink and the SSTI sink. Secondary hypothesis (NOT yet blackbox-confirmed, precondition must be proven before reporting): is_privileged is trusted straight from the Flask session cookie, signed with SECRET_KEY = "dev-only-not-for-prod", a static value hardcoded identically in build/docker-compose.yml -- if that key is ever disclosed (source leak, or read from the container post-RCE via the very SSTI sink this file guards) an attacker can forge a session with is_privileged=True and hit /admin/report-template directly, skipping /login and the LDAP-injection step entirely. No blackbox (pre-compromise) path to the key was identified in this pass -- prove/kill: check for any info-disclosure route or debug config that leaks SECRET_KEY without first achieving SSTI; if none exists, this is a persistence/re-entry primitive (survives an LDAP-side fix) rather than an initial-access one.
signals: authz decision trusts session cookie value directly
static SECRET_KEY shared across shipped deployment config
no blackbox key-disclosure path found yet

ranked_files.reason: Sink: uses plain jinja2.Environment (not SandboxedEnvironment) with no autoescape and no execution sandboxing whatsoever -- the ONLY control preventing arbitrary code execution is the flawed is_blocked() regex in app/ssti_blacklist.py. Once that blacklist is bypassed (confirmed above), this function has no independent defense layer -- full attacker-controlled Jinja2 template compiled and rendered.
signals: template compiled from raw user string
single point of failure for the blacklist

ranked_files.reason: Intended trust boundary: builds an LDAP search filter via str.format() with attacker-controlled username/password substituted directly into `(&(sAMAccountName={username})(info={password}))`, then treats any matching entry as a successful bind (authentication-by-search, not authentication-by-bind). This is the designed LDAP-injection sink -- no additional unintended flaw found here beyond the documented chain, but it remains the critical auth-boundary file and should stay high-priority for any reviewer validating the sanitize.py defense.

By-design weak sanitizer (commit message: 'add weak LDAP input sanitizer with fullwidth-bypass') -- strips ASCII `( ) * \` before translating fullwidth Unicode equivalents (（ ） ＊) back into their ASCII forms, so an attacker submitting fullwidth parens survives the strip step and is converted into a real LDAP metacharacter afterward. This is the INTENDED vulnerability enabling the designed auth-bypass chain, not a new finding -- flagged here only so downstream agents don't waste time re-deriving intent from the ordering bug.

Connection/bind wiring only -- server host, bind DN, and bind password come from trusted environment variables, not request input, so no direct injection sink here. Note LDAP_MODE defaults to "real" (not "mock") when unset, meaning a misconfigured deploy silently binds to a live DC rather than failing safe -- an operational/config risk, not a code-level exploitable bug.

Entry point that wires os.environ.get("FLASK_SECRET_KEY", "dev-only-not-for-prod") into create_app(). In the actual shipped deployment (build/docker-compose.yml) FLASK_SECRET_KEY is explicitly set to the same static string, so this file's fallback default never fires in practice -- the operative source of the predictable key is docker-compose.yml, not this file. Kept at 3 (not higher) because the file itself is inert; see app/webapp.py for the session-trust implication.
signals: hardcoded fallback secret (dead code in current deployment)
